title: Solomon Islands and Australia sign a new security treaty
seoTitle: Australia–Solomon Islands treaty: what the deal changes
dek: The agreement names Australia as Solomon Islands’ main security partner. It also commits Solomon Islands to keeping foreign military and security bases off its territory.
happened: Prime ministers Matthew Wale and Anthony Albanese signed the treaty in Canberra on November 25. It sets out closer ties on policing and border management and includes Australian support for education, infrastructure and visas. ABC News reports that Solomon Islands will consult Australia on national security and sensitive infrastructure.

sides.says: Wale said discussions with China were continuing. He cited a confidentiality clause when asked about the future of the existing agreement with Beijing.
Albanese said the treaty deepens security and economic ties. Australia has pledged support for Solomon Islands’ police force and wider access to work and training in Australia.

Foreign ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun said Beijing’s cooperation with Pacific countries was based on mutual respect. He did not directly answer whether Solomon Islands had told China it would end the pact.

next: Under the new treaty, Australia says it will expand police cooperation and improve visa arrangements. ABC News reports that Solomon Islands intends to let its separate pact with China lapse when it comes up for renewal in April 2027. Wale did not publicly confirm that report.
summary: Australia and Solomon Islands signed a treaty that deepens security and economic cooperation. Whether Solomon Islands will renew its separate pact with China remains publicly unconfirmed.
